rv.q: This is a meticulous and artfully conceived blend of storytelling, technology and actorly skill, running a tight 90 minutes.
This is a good, old-fashioned ghost-train of a story.
But horror theatre is a small, weird and often terrible genre and this is a proper scary little gem.
In any good rollercoaster ride, the achingly slow rise is at least as important as the 100mph hurtle that follows.
It's expertly atmospheric – a masterclass in staging horror slickly – and fortunately, its trappings are enough to excuse the slightly naff and overly familiar story.
Entertaining more than it was eerie, it was a thoughtful and satisfying experience.
Whether or not you believe in ghosts, this should prove at the very least a decent work out for your adrenal gland.
a bold, atmospheric piece that redefines how we experience theatre
Writer and director Jamie Armitage brings everything to a pleasing completion without over-explaining the mechanics.
The headphone gimmick might feel unnecessary, taking away rather than adding to the story, but even so A ghost In Your Ear still succeeds in delivering a fun spooky story with a few genuine scares.
The result is an absolutely outstanding production, and the first 5-star show of the year - one that will haunt you long after you leave the theatre.
Eerie and mesmerising, A Ghost in Your Ear feels much longer than a 90-minute thrill in the way in which it completely immerses the listener in the experience.
A Ghost In Your Ear is a good old fashioned story which encourages careful viewing and listening to deliver a very, very satisfying outcome.
